\section[la lampadina]{la lampadina — the light bulb}

\label{lesson:IT-C436-lampadina}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to cool down, then the Italian for the water heater.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la lampadina}
\textbf{la lampadina} — \textquotedblleft{}the light bulb\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
In bagno serve una lampadina nuova.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A new bulb is needed in the bathroom.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La lampada} is a lamp.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{lampadina} is a little \emph{lampada} 'lamp', which is inherited from Latin \emph{lampas}, from Greek \emph{lampás} 'torch' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la lampadina}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la lampadina}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la lampadina}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to cool down, then the Italian for the water heater, then say \emph{la lampadina} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la lampadina mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The light bulb\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[l'interruttore]{l'interruttore — the switch (for a light)}

\label{lesson:IT-C436-interruttore}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the water heater, then the Italian for the light bulb.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'interruttore}
\textbf{l'interruttore} — \textquotedblleft{}the switch (for a light)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
L'interruttore è dietro la porta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The switch is behind the door.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{interrompere}: it interrupts the current.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{interruttore} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{interruptor} 'an interrupter', from \emph{interrumpere} 'to break off', built on \emph{rumpere} 'to break' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'interruttore}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'interruttore}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'interruttore}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the water heater, then the Italian for the light bulb, then say \emph{l'interruttore} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does l'interruttore mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The switch (for a light)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[il fusibile]{il fusibile — the fuse}

\label{lesson:IT-C436-fusibile}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the light bulb, then the Italian for the switch.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il fusibile}
\textbf{il fusibile} — \textquotedblleft{}the fuse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
È saltato un fusibile.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A fuse has blown.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Saltare} is the verb: the fuse jumps.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fusibile} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{fūsibilis} 'that can be melted', from \emph{fundere} 'to pour, to melt' (Lewis \& Short): the wire melts and cuts the current.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il fusibile}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il fusibile}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il fusibile}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the light bulb, then the Italian for the switch, then say \emph{il fusibile} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does il fusibile mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The fuse\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ricaricare]{ricaricare — to recharge; to reload}

\label{lesson:IT-C436-ricaricare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the switch, then the Italian for the fuse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: ricaricare}
\textbf{ricaricare} — \textquotedblleft{}to recharge; to reload\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Devo ricaricare il telefono.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I need to charge my phone.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Il caricabatterie} — the charger.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ricaricare} is built from \emph{ri-} 'again' and \emph{caricare} 'to load', which is inherited from Late Latin \emph{carricāre}, built on \emph{carrus} 'cart'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ricaricare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ricaricare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ricaricare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the switch, then the Italian for the fuse, then say \emph{ricaricare} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does ricaricare mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To recharge; to reload\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[fulminarsi]{fulminarsi — to burn out (of a bulb)}

\label{lesson:IT-C436-fulminarsi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the fuse, then the Italian for to recharge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: fulminarsi}
\textbf{fulminarsi} — \textquotedblleft{}to burn out (of a bulb)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Si è fulminata la lampadina della cucina.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The kitchen bulb has burnt out.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fulminare} also means to strike with lightning, or with a look.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fulminarsi} is built on \emph{fulmine} 'lightning', which is inherited from Latin \emph{fulmen} 'thunderbolt' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fulminarsi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fulminarsi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{fulminarsi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the fuse, then the Italian for to recharge, then say \emph{fulminarsi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[(dialogue)]{Ripasso dei capitoli 429–436}

\label{lesson:IT-R436-ripasso-429-436}



\begin{quote}
Say the Italian for the hostel and the farm stay.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the hostel, the farm stay, the inn, the guesthouse, the campsite
  \item to pitch, the sleeping bag, the caravan, the camper van, the mosquito net
  \item the deposit, the advance, to cancel, the cancellation fee, to bring forward
  \item to lodge, to stay the night, the overnight stay, to stay, the porter
  \item double, the cot, the pillowcase, the bar of soap, the hair dryer
  \item the tap, to drip, blocked, the drain, to unblock
  \item the heating, the radiator, the air conditioner, to cool down, the water heater
  \item the light bulb, the switch, the fuse, to recharge, to burn out
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The hostel? (\textbf{l'ostello}.) The farm stay? (\textbf{l'agriturismo}.) The inn? (\textbf{la locanda}.) The guesthouse? (\textbf{la pensione}.) The campsite? (\textbf{il campeggio}.) To pitch? (\textbf{piantare}.) The sleeping bag? (\textbf{il sacco a pelo}.) The caravan? (\textbf{la roulotte}.) The camper van? (\textbf{il camper}.) The mosquito net? (\textbf{la zanzariera}.) The deposit? (\textbf{la caparra}.) The advance? (\textbf{l'acconto}.) To cancel? (\textbf{disdire}.) The cancellation fee? (\textbf{la penale}.) To bring forward? (\textbf{anticipare}.) To lodge? (\textbf{alloggiare}.) To stay the night? (\textbf{pernottare}.) The overnight stay? (\textbf{il pernottamento}.) To stay? (\textbf{soggiornare}.) The porter? (\textbf{il portiere}.) Double? (\textbf{matrimoniale}.) The cot? (\textbf{la culla}.) The pillowcase? (\textbf{la federa}.) The bar of soap? (\textbf{la saponetta}.) The hair dryer? (\textbf{l'asciugacapelli}.) The tap? (\textbf{il rubinetto}.) To drip? (\textbf{gocciolare}.) Blocked? (\textbf{intasato}.) The drain? (\textbf{lo scarico}.) To unblock? (\textbf{sturare}.) The heating? (\textbf{il riscaldamento}.) The radiator? (\textbf{il termosifone}.) The air conditioner? (\textbf{il condizionatore}.) To cool down? (\textbf{rinfrescare}.) The water heater? (\textbf{lo scaldabagno}.) The light bulb? (\textbf{la lampadina}.) The switch? (\textbf{l'interruttore}.) The fuse? (\textbf{il fusibile}.) To recharge? (\textbf{ricaricare}.) To burn out? (\textbf{fulminarsi}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
